gold.label: Together: the gold move

steps.say: 5 to 10 is half of the first bar (width 5).
10 to 20 is the whole second bar.
20 to 25 is a quarter of the third bar (width 5).

steps.done: About 75 items lie between 5 and 25. Splitting part-bars by width, then adding, is the gold skill.

gold.display: Estimate how many items are between 5 and 25 (dashed lines). Take the fraction of each bar's width that falls in the range. Split the end bars by width.

bronze.label: Together: your first one

steps.say: The median is the line inside the box.
IQR is the width of the box.
Range is whisker tip to whisker tip.
steps.done: Median 25, IQR 20, range 35, all read straight off the plot. That is the bronze skill.

bronze.display: Read the five-number summary from this box plot: median, Q1, Q3, then the IQR and range. Read each value off the scale.

silver.label: Together: the silver move

steps.say: First bar, 0 to 10: frequency = density × width.
Third bar, 20 to 40, is wider: width 20.

steps.done: The bars hold 100 items altogether. Density times width for each bar, then add, is the silver skill.

silver.display: This histogram has unequal class widths. Find the total frequency (frequency = density × width for each bar, then add). Areas, not heights, give the frequencies.

opener.label: Before any formulas

steps.pre: Which score is right in the middle, with four on each side?
steps.say: Nine test scores are lined up smallest to largest. No formulas, just point.
steps.hint: Count in from both ends until you meet in the middle.

steps.pre: Halfway between the middle two of those (5 and 6) is
steps.say: That middle value is the median. Now look only at the lower four: 3, 5, 6, 8.

You just found the median (the middle) and the lower quartile Q1 (the middle of the bottom half). The upper quartile Q3 is the middle of the top half. A box plot draws these five markers; a cumulative frequency curve finds them for hundreds of values by reading at n/2, n/4 and 3n/4. That is this whole lesson.

steps: Cumulative frequency: running totals plotted at the upper class boundary, joined with a smooth curve.
Read the median at n/2, Q1 at n/4, Q3 at 3n/4; IQR = Q3 − Q1.
Box plot: min, Q1, median, Q3, max. Range = max − min.
Histogram: frequency = frequency density × class width.
method_card.title: Cumulative Frequency, Box Plots & Histograms
method_card.content:
Cumulative frequency is a running total, plotted at the upper class boundary and joined with a smooth curve. Read the median at n/2, Q1 at n/4 and Q3 at 3n/4; IQR = Q3 − Q1.

A box plot shows five numbers: minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum. In a histogram, frequency density = frequency ÷ class width, so frequency = density × width, and the area of a bar equals its frequency.
method_card.example:
Box plot: min 15, Q1 25, median 35, Q3 50, max 70.

IQR = 50 − 25 = 25. Range = 70 − 15 = 55.

steps: Part of a histogram bar: take the fraction of the width you need. For 15 to 25 across bars of width 10, use 5 out of 10 of each bar's frequency.
Percentiles on a CF curve: 'top 20% pass' means 80% of students sit below the pass mark. Find the matching CF, then read the value.
Modal class = highest frequency density (tallest bar), not highest frequency. Compare distributions by median (average) and IQR (consistency).
gold.title: Gold: estimate and interpret

steps.label: Check
steps.content: Frequencies 60, 50, 40 do not decide it; density does ✓

example.question: A histogram: 0-20 (FD 3), 20-30 (FD 5), 30-50 (FD 2). Find the modal class.

steps: On a box plot, five marks show the minimum, lower quartile Q1, median, upper quartile Q3 and maximum. The median is the line inside the box.
Range = max − minimum. IQR = Q3 − Q1, the width of the box.
On a cumulative frequency curve, read the median at n/2, Q1 at n/4 and Q3 at 3n/4: up to the curve, then down to the value.
In a histogram, frequency = frequency density × class width.
bronze.title: Bronze: read a single value from a chart

steps.label: Check
steps.content: The box (14) is narrower than the range (30) ✓

example.question: A box plot shows min 4, Q1 12, median 18, Q3 26, max 34. Find the IQR.

steps: Histogram frequency: multiply the bar's density by its class width. Add several bars to get a total frequency.
Cumulative frequency between two values: read the CF at each end and subtract the smaller from the larger.
IQR uses the quartiles only: Q3 − Q1. The median sits between them but is not used.
silver.title: Silver: two steps to an answer

example.question: A histogram bar spans 20 to 40 with frequency density 3. Find the frequency.

gold.hint: 15 to 25 cuts across two bars. Take the matching fraction of each bar's width.
gold.display: The histogram shows ages of visitors. Estimate the number of visitors aged between 15 and 25.

guided_steps.pre: 15 to 20 is half of the 10 to 20 bar: FD 4 × width 5 =
guided_steps.say: 15 to 25 crosses two bars, so take half of each.

guided_steps.pre: 20 to 25 is half of the 20 to 30 bar: FD 3 × width 5 =
guided_steps.say: Now the second part.

guided_steps.pre: The whole 10 to 20 bar would be 4 × 10 =
guided_steps.done: The full bar is 40; we used only half (20), which is why we split. About 35 visitors. Correct.
guided_steps.hint: Full bar would be 40, we used half.

misconceptions.message: 70 uses the whole 10 to 20 and 20 to 30 bars. Only half of each lies in 15 to 25: 4 × 5 + 3 × 5 = 35.

gold.hint: 80% pass means 20% fail. Find the score where the cumulative frequency reaches those 20 students.
gold.display: The CF curve shows results for 100 students. The pass mark is set so that 80% of students pass. Estimate the pass mark from the graph.

guided_steps.say: 80% pass, so the pass mark sits above the bottom 20% who fail. Turn 20% into a number of students.

guided_steps.pre: Reading up from CF = 20, the score is
guided_steps.say: Find the score where the cumulative frequency reaches 20 (the 20 who fail sit below it).
guided_steps.hint: Across at 20, down to the score axis.

guided_steps.pre: Check: how many of the 100 are above 30? 100 − 20 =
guided_steps.done: 80 students (80%) score above 30, so 30 is the pass mark.

misconceptions.message: 80% pass, so 20% (20 students) fail. The pass mark is where CF = 20, giving 30. Reading at CF = 80 finds the top-20% boundary, not the pass mark.

gold.hint: The modal class has the highest frequency density (tallest bar), not the highest frequency.
gold.display: A histogram has bars: 0-10 (FD=2), 10-25 (FD=4), 25-30 (FD=8), 30-50 (FD=1.5). Find the modal class.

misconceptions.message: With unequal classes the modal class is the highest frequency density, not frequency. FD = 8 in 25 to 30 is tallest.

gold.hint: Work out each frequency (density times width), then find which class holds the middle value.
gold.display: A histogram: 0-20 (FD=3), 20-30 (FD=5), 30-50 (FD=2). Estimate the median class.

misconceptions.message: Frequencies are 3×20 = 60, 5×10 = 50, 2×20 = 40; total 150, so the median is the 75th value. Cumulative: 60, then 110, so the 75th lies in 20 to 30.

gold.hint: Compare the medians (the line inside each box) and subtract.
gold.display: Compare the two box plots. By how much does Group B's median exceed Group A's?

guided_steps.say: Compare the medians: the line inside each box.
Now Group B.

guided_steps.done: Adding 15 to A's median gives B's median. Correct.

misconceptions.message: 10 compares the upper quartiles (60 − 50). The question asks about the medians: 50 − 35 = 15.

bronze.hint: The median is at n/2. Read across from that cumulative frequency to the curve, then down.
bronze.display: The cumulative frequency curve shows test scores for 60 students. Read the median score from the graph.

guided_steps.say: The median splits the data in half. Find the halfway position first.
guided_steps.hint: Halve the total number of students.

guided_steps.say: Go up from cumulative frequency 30 to the curve, then read down to the score axis.
guided_steps.hint: Trace across at 30, then straight down.

guided_steps.pre: Check: students scoring above the median = 60 − 30 =
guided_steps.done: 30 below and 30 above confirms 45 is the middle.

misconceptions.message: 30 is the cumulative frequency you read across at, not the score. Go down to the x-axis: the median is about 45.

bronze.hint: IQR is the width of the box: upper quartile minus lower quartile.
bronze.display: The box plot shows exam results. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?

guided_steps.say: The IQR measures the middle 50%: the width of the box.
guided_steps.hint: The right-hand edge of the box.

guided_steps.say: Now the lower quartile.
guided_steps.hint: The left-hand edge of the box.

guided_steps.pre: Check it is smaller than the range: max − min = 75 − 20 =
guided_steps.done: 55 is the range; the box (IQR 25) is smaller, as it must be. Correct.
guided_steps.hint: The whole spread is bigger than the box.

misconceptions.message: 55 is the range (max − min). The IQR is the box width: Q3 − Q1 = 55 − 30 = 25.

bronze.hint: The median is the line inside the box, not the midpoint of the box.
bronze.display: The box plot shows heights of plants. What is the median height?

guided_steps.say: Do not average the edges: the median is a drawn line.
guided_steps.hint: Lower quartile, left edge of the box.

guided_steps.say: Now the line inside the box.
guided_steps.hint: The line between the two box edges.

guided_steps.done: The median (24) is the drawn line, not the box midpoint (25). Read the line.
guided_steps.hint: Average the edges to see they differ.

misconceptions.message: 25 is the midpoint of the box, (18 + 32) ÷ 2. The median is the line actually drawn inside: 24.

bronze.hint: Q1 is at n/4. Read across from that cumulative frequency to the curve, then down.
bronze.display: The cumulative frequency curve shows waiting times for 80 patients. Find Q1 (the lower quartile).

guided_steps.say: Q1 is a quarter of the way through the data. Find the quarter position.
Go up from cumulative frequency 20 to the curve, then down to the time axis.
guided_steps.hint: Trace across at 20, then straight down.

guided_steps.pre: Check: a quarter of the 80 patients is
guided_steps.done: 20 patients (a quarter) waited under 10 minutes, confirming Q1.

misconceptions.message: 20 is the cumulative frequency (n ÷ 4) you read across at, not the time. Read down to the axis: Q1 is about 10 minutes.

bronze.hint: Range is the full spread: maximum minus minimum.
bronze.display: The box plot shows weights of parcels. What is the range?

guided_steps.say: The range is the full spread, from smallest to largest.
Now the smallest value.

guided_steps.hint: Subtract the smallest from the largest.

guided_steps.pre: The IQR would be Q3 − Q1 = 30 − 15 =
guided_steps.done: 15 is the IQR (the box); the range (30) is the whole spread. Correct.

misconceptions.message: 15 is the IQR (Q3 − Q1, the box width). The range is the whole spread: max − min = 40 − 10 = 30.

bronze.hint: Frequency is the bar's area: frequency density times class width.
bronze.display: A histogram bar has frequency density 5 and class width 4. Find the frequency.

guided_steps.say: In a histogram, frequency is the area of the bar: density times width.
And the width of the class.

guided_steps.done: Dividing the frequency by the width gives back FD = 5. Correct.

misconceptions.message: 5 is the frequency density (the bar height). Multiply by the class width: 5 × 4 = 20.

bronze.hint: Frequency density = frequency divided by class width.
bronze.display: A histogram bar represents 24 items and has class width 8. Find the frequency density.

guided_steps.say: Frequency density undoes the area: divide the frequency by the class width.
And the width of the class.

guided_steps.done: Density times width returns the frequency 24. Correct.
guided_steps.hint: FD × width should give the frequency back.

misconceptions.message: 192 multiplies instead of dividing. FD = frequency ÷ width = 24 ÷ 8 = 3.

bronze.hint: IQR is the gap between the quartiles: Q3 minus Q1.
bronze.display: A box plot has Q1 = 28 and Q3 = 50. Find the IQR.

guided_steps.say: The IQR is the gap between the two quartiles.
And the lower quartile.

guided_steps.done: Adding the IQR back to Q1 returns Q3 = 50. Correct.
guided_steps.hint: Q1 plus the IQR should give Q3.

misconceptions.message: 78 adds the quartiles. The IQR subtracts them: Q3 − Q1 = 50 − 28 = 22.

silver.hint: More consistent means a smaller interquartile range (a narrower box).
silver.display: The two box plots compare Year 10 and Year 11. Which year group performed more consistently?

misconceptions.message: Consistent means less spread. Year 10's IQR is 55 − 40 = 15; Year 11's is 65 − 30 = 35. The smaller IQR (Year 10) is more consistent.

silver.hint: Read the cumulative frequency at each end, then subtract the smaller from the larger.
silver.display: The CF curve shows data for 120 students. Estimate the number of students who scored between 30 and 60.

guided_steps.say: Count how many fall below each end, then subtract.
guided_steps.hint: Up from 60 to the curve, across to the CF axis.

guided_steps.say: Now the lower end.
guided_steps.hint: Up from 30 to the curve, across.
Subtract the lower count from the higher.

guided_steps.done: Half the students fall in this middle band, which matches the curve. Correct.

misconceptions.message: 78 is the number up to 60. Subtract those up to 30 (18): 78 − 18 = 60.

silver.hint: Frequency is height times width, not just the height.
silver.display: The histogram shows journey times. How many people had a journey time between 10 and 20 minutes? (FD × class width = frequency)

guided_steps.say: Frequency is the bar's area: height times width, not just the height.
guided_steps.hint: The top of the 10 to 20 bar.

guided_steps.say: Now the width of that class.

guided_steps.done: Dividing back by the width returns the density 4. Correct.

misconceptions.message: 4 is the frequency density (the bar height). Multiply by the class width: 4 × 10 = 40.

silver.hint: IQR uses only the quartiles: Q3 minus Q1. Ignore the median.
silver.display: A CF curve shows Q1 = 35, median = 48, Q3 = 62. Find the IQR.

guided_steps.say: The IQR uses only the two quartiles, not the median.
And the lower quartile.

guided_steps.hint: Subtract Q1 from Q3, ignore the median.

guided_steps.done: Q1 plus the IQR returns Q3 = 62. Correct.

misconceptions.message: 14 subtracts the median (Q3 − median). The IQR uses the quartiles: Q3 − Q1 = 62 − 35 = 27.

silver.hint: Turn each density into a frequency (density times width), then add them all.
silver.display: A histogram has classes 0-5 (FD=3), 5-10 (FD=5), 10-20 (FD=4), 20-40 (FD=1). Find the total frequency.

guided_steps.say: Turn each density into a frequency (density times width), then add.
guided_steps.hint: Density times width for the first bar.

guided_steps.say: The second bar.
The third bar is wider: width 10.

guided_steps.done: The four bars represent 100 items in total (the area under the histogram).

misconceptions.message: 13 adds the frequency densities. Add the frequencies (density × width): 15 + 25 + 40 + 20 = 100.

silver.hint: Higher average means a bigger median; more consistent means a smaller IQR.
silver.display: Box plot A: median 60, IQR 15. Box plot B: median 55, IQR 25. Which statement is correct?
options: A has a higher average and is more consistent
B has a higher average but A is more consistent
A is better in every way

misconceptions.message: A's median (60) beats B's (55), so A has the higher average; A's IQR (15) is smaller than B's (25), so A is more consistent too.

silver.hint: The cumulative frequency counts values below. Those above = total minus that count.
silver.display: From a CF diagram with 200 data points, estimate how many are above 70 if CF at 70 is 150.

guided_steps.pre: How many are at most 70? CF =
guided_steps.say: The cumulative frequency tells you how many are below a value. Above it is the rest.
And the total number of data points.

guided_steps.hint: Subtract the cumulative frequency from the total.

guided_steps.done: Below plus above adds back to the total 200. Correct.
guided_steps.hint: The two parts should give the total.

misconceptions.message: 150 is the number up to 70. Those above 70 = total − 150 = 200 − 150 = 50.

problem_bank.gold_description: Estimate across parts of bars, work with percentiles, find modal or median classes, and compare distributions.
problem_bank.bronze_description: Read one value from a box plot or cumulative frequency curve, or do a single frequency density step.
problem_bank.silver_description: Take two steps: frequencies from a histogram, differences from a cumulative frequency curve, or an IQR.
